title: 1 Peter
lead: The first letter in Peter's name, sent from 'Babylon' (probably Rome) to believers, probably mostly Gentile, scattered across five regions of Asia Minor. It calls them chosen 'temporary residents', gives them Israel's titles, and teaches them to do good and hope under slander and suffering, following Christ, who suffered unjustly and now rules over every power.

sections.b: The letter names Peter the apostle as its author and Silvanus as the one 'through' whom he wrote (1:1; 5:12), as secretary or as courier. Traditional readers date it to the 60s, before Peter's death in Rome; many scholars see it as the work of a Petrine circle in Rome later in the first century. It was accepted early and widely: Polycarp echoes it, and Eusebius lists it among the books all acknowledged.

Christ's proclamation 'to the spirits in prison' (3:19) and 'the good news was announced even to the dead' (4:6), the baptism that 'saves you now as well' (3:21), 'a royal priesthood' (2:9), and the household code for slaves and wives (2:18-3:7).
